description.narrative: The proposed action will deliver on the EU commitments under the ¿EU-Nigeria Digital Economy Package¿[1] (2024 GG Flagship project) and will support the implementation of the government 2024 Digital Economy and E-Governance Bill. It will target (i) further investments in connectivity to contribute to the roll out of 90,000 km of fibre-optic cable and (ii) digital overhaul of public governance and services, as well as (iii) foster talent necessary for the success and sustainability of such investments in line with the government 3 Million Technical Talent (3MTT) programme.[1] Adopted in 2022 under the Global Gateway Strategy and announced during Commission¿s VP Vestager visit in February that year, the Package supports Nigeria¿s digital transformation with EUR 820 M, combining EUR 160 M in grants and EUR 660 M in loans, covering the whole territory of Nigeria. The package aims at positioning the EU as a key partner of Nigeria in the provision of digital connectivity, e-governance solutions and digital skills. It fosters human-centred investments and job creation, taking into account inclusion as well as respect of fundamental human rights. The roll out of the Package is coordinated with EU Member States (notably Informal Digital Hub including: DE, FR, DK, FR, NL, FI, SE, etc.), EU DFIs (EIB, AFD), and the EU private sector (D4D Hub, and EU companies on the ground). It is also coordinated with, and complemented by, a number of regional level EU projects and facilities (D4D Hub, AEDIB, D4GOV/DIF, etc.). Implementation is being rolled out with EUR 550 million in EIB loans including the expected operation with the Development Bank of Nigeria and above EUR 110 million in grants through digital components to our MIP and regional programmes. In addition, there are upcoming investments in fiber optic cables
